The intake records continuous vulnerability scanning via Snyk and AWS Inspector, an annual third-party penetration test, and a critical-patch remediation SLA of seven days, establishing a documented vulnerability management and testing program. The intake records a 24/7 SOC operated by a managed security service provider (MSSP) and an active intrusion detection system (IDS), with a maturity of {{SAFEGUARDS:list}}, establishing a documented and continuously operated network monitoring and defense program. The intake does not name the MSSP, specify the IDS tooling, or describe the escalation and response protocol between the MSSP SOC and internal teams, which the auditor may require to assess the adequacy of the monitoring arrangement.

This control shares the '{{SAFEGUARDS:list}}' maturity designation with the encryption control, distinguishing both from the '{{SAFEGUARDS_2:list}}' controls; however, unlike the encryption control — which names specific tooling (AES-256, TLS 1.3, AWS KMS) — the network monitoring control names neither the MSSP nor the IDS product, making the unnamed MSSP and IDS the specific artefact gap that limits the score relative to the encryption control.

The intake documents a formal enterprise threat-intelligence program, membership in the Retail & Hospitality ISAC and MS-ISAC, monthly threat briefs circulated to engineering and product teams, and quarterly CISO briefings to the executive team — collectively constituting an active, multi-channel awareness program directed at both technical staff and leadership. The business must retain documentation that separately evidences these awareness activities — such as threat advisory distribution records, ISAC membership confirmations, and CISO briefing agendas or minutes — distinct from formal training curricula, so that the auditor can assess the {{MODULE}} awareness and {{MODULE}} education and training components independently.

This control is distinguished from the {{MODULE}} education and training control by its multi-channel, continuous threat-intelligence distribution model — ISAC membership, monthly briefs, and executive briefings — rather than a structured annual curriculum, reflecting a higher evidentiary breadth for ongoing awareness than the single-cadence training artifact.

This control scores modestly below the {{MODULE}} awareness control because it rests on two artifacts — annual training and quarterly phishing simulations — without specifying role-based or engineering-specific curricula, whereas the awareness control documents a richer, multi-channel distribution program with named external memberships and executive-level touchpoints.

{{CITE_1:cite}} The mean score of 82 across all 18 scored components places the organization in the Substantially Ready band. Every component is rated Implemented, with scores ranging from 77 (antivirus and anti-malware protections) to 88 (oversight of service providers, contractors, and third parties). No control falls below the Implemented threshold, and no Gap or Critical Gap findings exist on this record. The {{FRAMEWORK}} primary framework, documented within the last 12 months, provides a substantive audit-evidence foundation that the independent auditor can leverage. Three incremental evidence-readiness priorities emerge from the record: first, confirming that the Datadog audit-log deployment documents the specific systems and event types covered; second, confirming that CrowdStrike coverage extends to server and cloud workload endpoints in addition to end-user devices; and third, confirming that the authentication control's documentation captures session-management and adaptive-risk policies beyond the core Okta MFA and SSO configuration. No incidents were reported in the last 12 months.
